summary: This standards-track document registers the mailserver: URI scheme as historic in the IANA registry. The scheme was defined long ago for pointing to mail servers but was never meaningfully used, so it should not be used in new software. Marking it historic tells people it is retired.

plainLanguage.summary: Years ago someone made a special kind of web address for mail servers, but nobody used it. This document puts a sign on it saying it is retired.

questions: what is the mailserver uri scheme
is the mailserver uri scheme historic
what replaces the mailserver uri scheme
subtitle: Retires the vague mailserver: URI scheme by registering it as Historic.

tldr.problem: RFC 1738 registered the mailserver: URI scheme with only the description "Access to data available from mail servers" and no details, so it is not interoperable.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6196 discourages any future implementation and asks IANA to re-register the scheme as Historic in the URI scheme registry.
tldr.outcome: The scheme is now marked Historic. Implementors should use mailto:, imap:, pop: or http: URIs instead.

today: RFC 6196 updates RFC 1738 and records the mailserver: URI scheme as Historic in the IANA registry. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Why the Scheme Is Retired
sections.content:
RFC 1738 registered the mailserver: URI scheme as provisional in the IANA URI registry, describing it only as "Access to data available from mail servers". No further details were provided, and the author knew of no more detailed definition. As specified, the scheme is not interoperable.

There is a small risk that someone would implement it from the registry entry alone and invent undocumented syntax. To minimize that risk, the document discourages future implementations and asks IANA to mark the scheme Historic. Earlier attempts to document it in detail were not successful.
sections.plainLanguage: Nobody ever wrote down how this address type works, so anyone using it would be guessing. Retiring it stops people from guessing in different ways.

sections.title: What to Use Instead
sections.content: For instructions to generate an email message, implementors can use the mailto: URI scheme from RFC 6068. To reference a message or set of messages in a mailstore, they can use the imap: scheme (RFC 5092), the pop: scheme (RFC 2384) or http: URIs (RFC 2616).
sections.plainLanguage: If you want to write an email, use the mailto kind of link. If you want to point at stored mail, use the imap, pop or http kinds of link.

sections.title: IANA and Security Considerations
sections.content:
IANA has re-registered the mailserver: URI scheme as Historic in the URI scheme registry and updated the reference to point to this document. This updates RFC 1738.

The security section notes the scheme was never properly documented and so does not interoperate, and that there are no known implementations of it.
sections.plainLanguage: The official list now says this address type is retired. There is no known software that uses it, so nothing breaks.
